title: Extend usage aggregation to 7/14/30-day windows for PLG→Sales signals (spend, tokens, concurrency, errors)
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Context
We need reliable, low-latency usage windows (7/14/30d) to power v1 PLG→Sales triggers. The scoring service will consume pre-aggregated windows rather than scanning raw events.

Scope (v1)
Build/extend daily and near-real-time aggregation jobs that produce 7/14/30-day rolling metrics per workspace/account, and publish into analytics tables consumed by the signal scoring service.

Metrics required (per workspace_id, per day; also maintain latest snapshot)
1) Spend (USD)
- billable_usd_7d / 14d / 30d
- hosted_api_usd_7d / 14d / 30d (if split is available from billing line items)
- free_credit_usd_applied_7d / 14d / 30d (for guardrails / analysis; not required for routing)

2) Tokens
- input_tokens_7d / 14d / 30d
- output_tokens_7d / 14d / 30d
- total_tokens_7d / 14d / 30d
- requests_7d / 14d / 30d

3) Concurrency / bursts
- p95_concurrent_requests_7d / 14d / 30d (computed over 5-min buckets)
- max_concurrent_requests_7d / 14d / 30d
- burst_events_7d / 14d / 30d (count of 5-min buckets above threshold; threshold defined in scoring service config)

4) Errors / friction signals
- http_429_count_7d / 14d / 30d
- http_5xx_count_7d / 14d / 30d
- model_routing_failure_count_7d / 14d / 30d (capacity/fallback/compat failures)
- rate_limit_rejections_7d / 14d / 30d (if distinct from 429)
- error_rate_7d / 14d / 30d (errors / requests)

Data sources
- request logs / telemetry stream: per-request tokens, status code, model, workspace_id, request_id, timestamp
- billing ledger: daily spend per workspace_id (or line items with timestamps)
- quota/rate limit events: optional if not fully captured by 429s

Tables (proposed)
- analytics.workspace_usage_daily (partition by day): daily aggregates (tokens, requests, error counts, concurrency buckets)
- analytics.workspace_usage_windows (partition by day): rolling 7/14/30 window columns
- analytics.workspace_usage_latest (no partition): latest available window snapshot per workspace_id for low-latency reads

Notes
- Concurrency is computed from 5-minute buckets (count of in-flight or concurrent request starts within bucket). Use the existing bucketed telemetry table if available; otherwise compute from request start/end events where possible.
- Window refresh cadence: windows recomputed hourly for the last 3 days, daily backfill for 30 days (per telemetry thread decision). This keeps latency low without expensive full recompute.
- Late arrivals: accept up to 48h of late telemetry; recompute daily partitions for D-1 and D-2.

Acceptance criteria
- For a sampled set of workspaces, windows match ground truth queries over raw request logs within +/-1% for tokens/requests and exact for billing ledger totals (billing is authoritative).
- Job completes within 45 minutes for daily run; hourly incremental run within 15 minutes.
- Data availability: windows table updated by 08:00 UTC daily; hourly snapshots updated within 90 minutes of wall-clock time.
- Metrics are documented (column definitions + caveats) and shared with scoring service owner (Nadia Rahman).

Implementation plan
1) Extend daily aggregate job to materialize the required base facts per workspace/day (tokens, requests, error counts, bucketed concurrency stats).
2) Build windowed rollup job (SQL) using base facts; write into workspace_usage_windows.
3) Create workspace_usage_latest as a view or small table updated each run (for fast reads).
4) Backfill last 90 days into daily table and last 60 days of windows (windows require 30-day lookback + buffer).
5) Add validation queries + monitoring checks (row counts, null rates, spend totals parity).

Open questions
- Do we treat ‘workspace’ as the account entity for HubSpot routing, or do we need domain/company mapping at this stage? (Assumption: scoring service handles enrichment; this ticket stays workspace-level.)
- Final definition of model_routing_failure (which telemetry codes qualify) — align with Logan/Nadia before freezing.

Links
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/plg-to-sales-signal-routing-prd.json
- Design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/signal-scoring-and-routing-design.json
- Related ticket: ENG-2842 (scoring + dedupe)
comments: 2025-02-05 (Nadia Rahman): Please ensure spend comes from billing ledger, not derived from tokens, to avoid mismatch when pricing changes or credits apply. Also add columns for free credit applied so Sales Ops can analyze false positives later (even if scoring doesn’t use it in v1).

2025-02-06 (Caleb Johnson): For error-rate signals, include both raw counts (429, 5xx) and computed error_rate. Scoring will likely use thresholds on 429_count and error_rate to avoid spiky denominators.

2025-02-07 (Mei Lin): Draft schema ready. Concurrency: we can compute p95/max from existing 5-min bucket table in warehouse; will not attempt request-level in-flight reconstruction. Will document caveat: counts are based on starts-per-bucket, not true concurrent in-flight.

2025-02-10 (Logan Wright): Aligning with eng-platform thread—hourly recompute for last 3 days + daily recompute for last 30 days. Keep the compute predictable; we’ll accept up to ~90 min lag for hourly snapshots.

2025-02-12 (Rafael Mendes): Add a basic anomaly check: alert if total rows per day drop >30% WoW, or if null rates for billable_usd exceed 1% of active workspaces. Link the future alert to ENG-2845 runbooks.

2025-02-14 (Mei Lin): Backfill kicked off for last 90 days; ETA 6 hours. Validation queries running on 50 sampled workspaces from pilot cohort list. Billing parity looks good; token parity within 0.6% median drift, 1.4% p95 (likely late arrivals).
2025-02-18 (Mei Lin): Shipped + merged. Latest snapshot table is updated hourly; added notes in table comments about late-arrival handling. Handed off column list + sample queries to ENG-2842.
